FIXUP: UPSTREAM: phy: rockchip-emmc: Set phyctrl_frqsel based on card clock --- NOTE --- This is a squash of a revert of commit 2668a3052de9 ("FROMLIST: phy: rockchip-emmc: Set phyctrl_frqsel based on card clock") with a re-pick from what landed upstream in Ulf's tree. --- NOTE --- The "phyctrl_frqsel" is described in the Arasan datasheet [1] as "the frequency range of DLL operation". Although the Rockchip variant of this PHY has different ranges than the reference Arasan PHY it appears as if the functionality is similar. We should set this phyctrl field properly. Note: as per Rockchip engineers, apparently the "phyctrl_frqsel" is actually only useful in HS200 / HS400 modes even though the DLL itself it used for some purposes in all modes. See the discussion in the earlier change in this series: ("mmc: sdhci-of-arasan: Always power the PHY off/on when clock changes"). In any case, it shouldn't hurt to set this always. Note that this change should allow boards to run at HS200 / HS400 speed modes while running at 100 MHz or 150 MHz. In fact, running HS400 at 150 MHz (giving 300 MB/s) is the main motivation of this series, since performance is still good but signal integrity problems are less prevelant at 150 MHz. [1]: https://arasan.com/wp-content/media/eMMC-5-1-Total-Solution_Rev-1-3.pdf BUG=chrome-os-partner:53445 TEST=Stress eMMC Change-Id: Idde5d824d3a45ae0928447fb84c9ded047376c59 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Acked-by: Kishon Vijay Abraham I <kishon@ti.com> Reviewed-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de> Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org> (cherry picked from git://git.linaro.org/people/ulf.hansson/mmc.git next commit a8ec3bbced6290772cdbd2b10a44190fda41b11a) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/356182 Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

cr50: enable highsec jittery clock The highsec jittery clock was breaking the USB peripheral, because it would use bank values that mapped to frequencies less than 15MHz. This change modifies stepx16 to keep the bankvalues mapped to frequencies above 18MHz to ensure the USB peripheral can work with the high security jittery clock.
